title: Phase 2: cloud substrate fan-out
description: Needs planning: one worker sandbox per tick; substrate=cloud in runners.toml behind the same spawn/wait/collect/reconcile contract; tk cloud verbs so local orchestrators drive cloud workers (D19); reconcile-on-reboot; run_event producers feeding ProjectRoom; R2 artifact streaming (harness.log during the run, never export-at-exit).
notes:
2026-08-19 21:47 - [human] Scope (human, 2026-08-19): benchmark sandbox start behaviour as soon as real sandboxes run. Phase 1 boots the FIRST real sandbox, Phase 2 makes it per-tick — which is exactly where start cost multiplies by fan-out width, so the numbers are load-bearing here rather than nice-to-have.

Measure at least:
- COLD: no sandbox, image not pulled — time to first useful work (this is the number that prices image size).
- WARM: sandbox asleep, image pulled and filesystem persisted — wake time.
- HOT: sandbox already running.
- Breakdown within each: image pull, container start, clone, toolchain provisioning (first run for a project), dependency install with a cold vs warm cache.
- FAN-OUT: N parallel sandboxes at N = 1, 3, 5 — does per-sandbox start time degrade, and where does the knee sit relative to orchestration.max_parallel.
- COST per run alongside wall-clock; spend is the other half of the decision and AI Gateway telemetry (k2s) makes it attributable.

Decisions these numbers should settle, all currently resting on assumption:
1. Whether the batteries-included ~2GB image is the right trade, or whether cold start argues for a thinner base plus provisioning. 3q2 was told to state this cost honestly; a benchmark replaces the assertion with a number.
2. Whether named sandboxes that sleep/wake genuinely amortise the image pull, which is the entire premise of keeping caches in the persistent sandbox rather than the image.
3. Whether per-repo warm setup (79x's [sandbox] setup key) earns its complexity.

Method note: publish the harness and the raw numbers, not just conclusions, and re-measure after any image or base change — this is a dated measurement against one platform, not a constant.
2026-08-21 14:36 - Phase 2 starts on branch epic/1vn, cut from main after Phase 1 landed (PR 50 carried epic/ko8; PR 51 carries the closeout remainder). Wave 1 is the three defects the measured runs found that make every later Phase 2 measurement wrong if left in: kji (wave width ignored — a benchmark of fan-out is meaningless while the configured width is not honoured), uzx (every trip condition sampled on a backing-off timer) and l4l (tk cloud trace — without it, diagnosing a run means hand-writing gateway API scripts, which is how the last three findings were actually found). Order matters: kuf and 0ds must not run before kji, because they measure concurrency.
acceptance_criteria: A single cloud run of an epic with at least 3 ready ticks fans out to one worker CONTAINER per tick (not subagents in one sandbox), and at least 3 of those tick branches come back ready-to-merge. Every worker reaches a real model turn on a Workers AI model through the factory gateway — zero exit-7 boots. A second wave of the same run also fans out to containers. `tk cloud logs <run>` prints each worker container's own output, so a failed worker is diagnosable without paying for another run. Green: go build ./..., go test ./..., node scripts/check-public-repo.mjs, and the factory + UI vitest suites.
